title: Deep learning mines antimicrobial peptides from the human gut microbiome
summary: An NLP-style pipeline (LSTM, attention, BERT) flagged 2,349 candidate antimicrobial peptides in gut microbiome data; 216 were synthesized and 181 showed activity, and the 11 most potent were effective against resistant Gram-negative pathogens, including a mouse lung infection model. Abstract-level review only; clinical relevance untested.
ai_technology: LSTM, attention and BERT neural pipeline

evidence.tested: 216 candidates synthesized, 181 active (>83%); 11 potent peptides tested; mouse bacterial lung infection model.
evidence.unknown: Toxicity, pharmacokinetics and human efficacy not assessed in the abstract; full text not read.
evidence.ai_role: Neural language models ranked candidate AMPs from metagenome sequences; wet-lab tests validated them.
